title: Bowel obstruction and ileus in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the bowel obstruction or ileus (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting.

Vitals:
T: 98.4 F, HR: 78, BP: 132/80, RR: 16, SpO2: 96% RA.

Recent Labs:
WBC: 11.2, Hgb: 13.4, Hct: 40.2, Na: 138, K: 4.1, Cr: 1.1, eGFR: 52, Glucose: 115.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Fatigue. GI: Nausea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain. MSK: Mild lower back pain. Neuro: Alert and oriented x3. No chest pain, SOB, or focal neuro deficits.

Social History: Retired, lives with wife. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol.

Family History: Father had HTN. Mother had T2DM.

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 90 y.o. male admitted for acute abdominal symptoms. Imaging confirmed a partial small bowel obstruction. The etiology of the obstruction is identified as adhesions from a prior abdominal surgery. Pt was started on NPO status and serial abdominal exams. A nasogastric tube was placed for decompression. Pt tolerated bowel rest well. Serial exams showed decreased distension and improved bowel sounds. Transitioned to clear liquids, then advanced diet as tolerated. Obstruction resolved. Pt stable for discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Partial small bowel obstruction, adhesions.

Discharge Medications:
1. Metformin 500mg BID
2. Lisinopril 10mg QD
3. Multivitamin QD

Follow-up:
F/u with PCP in 1 week for wound check and symptom monitoring.

Electronically signed,
L. Moreau, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Intestinal adhesions with partial obstruction: K56.51 (HCC 78).
